question:
These are the events that have already occurred:

...
94. Pascal asked the inspector for a trial.
95. Pascal fell on his knees and prayed earnestly.
96. Pascal resolved to cast out his meals from his cell window.
97. Pascal heard a scratching noise coming from the wall of his cell.
98. Pascal drank the soup brought by the jailer and regained strength.


Below is a list of possible subsequent events:

['Pascal devoured the fresh provisions brought by the jailer.', 'Pascal feasted on the delicious rations supplied by the jailer.', 'Pascal savored the rare delicacies delivered by the jailer.', 'Pascal relished the gourmet dishes provided by the jailer.', 'Pascal consumed the exquisite meals presented by the jailer.', 'Pascal enjoyed the lavish spread offered by the jailer.']

 Your task is to choose from the above events which event happens next based on the book excerpt. In your response to me, only include the answer without anything else.
references: Pascal devoured the fresh provisions brought by the jailer.

  (part 4 of 4) at his disposal.

He could hang himself with his handkerchief to the window bars, or refuse food and die of starvation.

But the first was repugnant to him.

Pascal had always entertained the greatest horror of pirates, who are hung up to the yard-arm; he would not die by what seemed an infamous death.

He resolved to adopt the second, and began that day to carry out his resolve.

Nearly four years had passed away; at the end of the second he had ceased to mark the lapse of time.

Pascal said, "I wish to die," and had chosen the manner of his death, and fearful of changing his mind, he had taken an oath to die.

"When my morning and evening meals are brought," thought he, "I will cast them out of the window, and they will think that I have eaten them."

He kept his word; twice a day he cast out, through the barred aperture, the provisions his jailer brought him -- at first gayly, then with deliberation, and at last with regret.

Nothing but the recollection of his oath gave him strength to proceed.

Hunger made viands once repugnant, now acceptable; he held the plate in his hand for an hour at a time, and gazed thoughtful
